themes.name: Colonialism and Imperialism
themes.description: The book critiques European colonialism in Africa, portraying it as a brutal, exploitative enterprise driven by greed for ivory and power, masked by hollow ideals of civilization and progress.

themes.name: Darkness and the Human Soul
themes.description: The journey into the Congo symbolizes a descent into the primal, savage aspects of human nature, revealing the capacity for evil and moral decay when removed from societal constraints.

themes.name: Madness and Isolation
themes.description: Kurtz's descent into madness illustrates how isolation in the wilderness, combined with unchecked power and greed, can corrupt and unravel the human psyche.

themes.name: Hypocrisy of Civilization
themes.description: The contrast between the lofty rhetoric of European 'civilizing missions' and the actual brutality and exploitation in the colonies exposes the hypocrisy at the heart of imperialist ideology.

themes.name: The Wilderness as a Force
themes.description: The African wilderness is depicted as a vast, indifferent, and vengeful presence that overwhelms and consumes those who invade it, stripping away pretense and revealing inner truths.

themes.name: Greed and Exploitation
themes.description: The relentless pursuit of ivory drives the narrative, showing how greed dehumanizes both the colonizers and the colonized, reducing people and land to mere resources.

themes.name: The Meaning of Work
themes.description: Marlow's focus on the practical tasks of navigating and repairing his steamboat serves as a counterpoint to the abstract ideals and moral decay, suggesting that honest work provides a grounding purpose.

themes.name: Silence and Communication
themes.description: The pervasive silence of the jungle and the fragmented, whispered conversations among the characters highlight the failure of language to convey the true horror and meaning of the colonial experience.
